Question: In an existing Agent/Chat, the user edits the FIRST user message (the original task bubble), deletes its text, types a completely new task into that same first input, and sends it. Does the current chat context reset so the model no longer sees the previous turns? Is that the same as opening a brand-new chat?

Please cover:
1. What Cursor does when you edit and resubmit an earlier user message (truncate/fork, what history is sent to the model).
2. Specifically if the edited message is the first message in the thread.
3. What is NOT reset: same chat id, sidebar thread, files already changed on disk, checkpoints, rules/skills/MCP, selected model.
4. Whether merely editing the text without pressing send changes context.
5. Any official doc URL.

Return a concise factual answer with certainty level and doc links. Do not modify anything.

content.text:
**No. Resubmitting a rewritten first message drops the old turns from that thread, but it is not a new chat.**

Certainty: **high** for truncation, the file dialog, and “not a new chat.” **Medium** for the conversation UUID, which the docs never say changes. Checked against Cursor docs on 2026-11-02 (IDE release notes through 3.27). There is no separate rule for the first bubble.

### 1. Edit and resubmit
Clicking an earlier user message only opens it for editing. **Enter / Send** resubmits it.

Cursor then **truncates in place**: every message after the edited one is removed, and the model is given the edited text plus whatever still precedes it. Later replies and tool results are not kept so they can contradict the new prompt.

If files changed after that message, Cursor asks **“Revert files to this message?”** and says later messages are removed either way:

- **Revert Files** (Enter) restores the checkpoint from that point.
- **Keep Files** (Shift+Enter) leaves the working tree as it is.

In **Ask** mode there is no file dialog and files are not reverted. Message truncation still happens.

This is not a branch. **Fork** is what copies the thread into a new chat. Forking from one message copies history through that message and drops everything after it, including later subagents.

### 2. First message
Same rule. Nothing in the thread comes before that bubble, so after you delete its text, type a new task, and send, the history sent to the model is **only the new user message**, plus the normal per-request envelope (system prompt, tools, rules, skills, MCP). The model does **not** see the previous turns.

It can still read the repo. With **Keep Files**, those old edits are still on disk. With **Revert Files**, the workspace rolls back to the snapshot at that first message. A brand-new chat never does that rollback.

### 3. What is not reset
- **Same sidebar thread.** The transcript is rewritten in place. Fork, or a new chat, is a different conversation. Docs do not say the conversation id is rotated.
- **Files**, unless you choose Revert Files. Ask mode never reverts them.
- **Checkpoints** are refreshed for this resubmit, not discarded as a system. Restoring a checkpoint by itself only reverts files and does **not** delete messages. Checkpoints are local and are not Git.
- **Rules, skills, and MCP** are injected again on the new request. They are not conversation history, and editing a message does not turn them off. While the bubble is open, `/` still lists skills.
- **Selected model** stays on this chat. While editing, Cmd+/ (Mac) changes the model for that message. It does not jump back to your account default.

Also not the same as a new chat: a new chat would not offer to revert files, and it would not delete this thread. Conversation search across other chats is a separate index. Docs do not say this edit purges that index.

### 4. Edit without Send
**No context change.** Typing in the bubble does not truncate history. Truncation and the revert dialog happen on resubmit. Escape leaves edit mode. In 3.21, Escape only closes an open model picker and does not cancel the edit.

### 5. Docs
- [IDE release notes, 3.19 and 3.21](https://cursor.com/docs/release-notes/ide) — revert dialog, “later messages are removed either way,” edited text is what gets sent, checkpoints refresh
- [Checkpoints](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/overview#checkpoints) — restore files only; messages stay
- [Undo Agent changes](https://cursor.com/help/ai-features/agent#how-do-i-undo-agent-changes) — fork to shorten the conversation
- [Fork vs side chat](https://cursor.com/help/ai-features/side-chats)
- [Context and model](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/prompting) — history, rules, skills, MCP, model stays for this chat
- [Rules in every mode](https://cursor.com/help/ai-features/agent#do-rules-apply-in-all-modes)

Staff descriptions that match this, not docs: [edit replaces later messages](https://forum.cursor.com/t/accidentally-editing-old-chat-message-wipes-context-after/170393) (2026-09-03) and [rewind vs fork](https://forum.cursor.com/t/rewinding-truncating-chat/171396) (2026-09-12).
